source_context_translations.translation: The nameless is the beginning of Heaven and Earth; the named is the mother of the ten thousand things.
Therefore, always without desire, one may observe its subtlety.
Always with desire, one may observe its outer limit.
These two come forth together but are named differently; together they are called the mysterious.
When everyone under heaven knows beauty as beauty, there is then ugliness.
He practices a teaching without words; the ten thousand things arise, and he does not refuse them; he gives them life without possessing them, acts without relying on them,
accomplishes merit and does not dwell on it.
Indeed, because he does not dwell on it, therefore it does not depart.

He does not exalt the worthy, so that the people do not contend; he does not prize goods hard to obtain, so that the people do not steal; he does not display what can be desired, so that the people’s hearts are not disturbed.
He causes the wise people not to dare to act.

The Way is empty, yet use of it will not fill it up; so deep—seems to be the ancestor of all things. It blunts its sharpness, untangles its confusions, tempers its light, and joins itself to the dust; so deep—seems somehow to exist.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): marks existence or presence, introducing something as extant or available
additional_senses.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text (Wang Bi recension)
Sentence Translations (English): There is a tiger in the mountains.
There is a tree in the courtyard.
There is a guest in the room.
There is order in the world.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): indicates ownership, possession, or being in a state of having something
additional_senses.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text (Wang Bi recension)
Sentence Translations (English): The ruler has a state.
A person has virtue.
I have a carriage.
He has talent.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): describes something as possessing a name or being designated by a name, rather than merely existing
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text (Wang Bi recension)

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): marks the instrument, method, or means by which something is done
additional_senses.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text (Wang Bi recension)
Sentence Translations (English): The ruler acts by ritual.
The minister remonstrates with words.
The craftsman works the wood with a knife.
The gentleman transforms the people by virtue.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): connects a cause or condition with its consequence
additional_senses.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text (Wang Bi recension)
Sentence Translations (English): The weather is cold; therefore, approach it with fire.
The matter is urgent; thus, many should act together.
The way is long; thus, it is completed over time.
The people are at peace; therefore, the state is secure.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): marks the purpose or intended result of an action
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text (Wang Bi recension)
contextual_sense.Translation (English): in order to; so as to

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): means to look for or pursue something by going after it
additional_senses.Register (English): Classical Chinese; literary; received text tradition
Sentence Translations (English): The gentleman enters the mountains to seek immortality.
The officer goes out at night to search for thieves.
A man travels far to seek profit.
The gentleman does not court good fortune through danger.
additional_senses.Translation (English): to seek; to go in search of

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): refers to a frontier post or the official who guards a border
additional_senses.Register (English): Classical Chinese; literary
Sentence Translations (English): The frontier posts were solemn and orderly.
The garrison is stationed at the border.
The carriage went out through the southern border.
At night the sentries patrol the frontier.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): refers to what appears at the edge or outward limit of something, the visible boundary or outward display
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): in Laozi, paired with 內/妙 as the outward side of a thing
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text (Wang Bi recension)

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): a noun-forming particle used after a verb or adjective phrase to make a person or thing identified by that description
additional_senses.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text (Wang Bi recension)
Sentence Translations (English): Those who know are few.
Those who are humane are at ease.
Those who are good follow.
Those who are brave advance.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): used after a demonstrative to pick out a thing or category just mentioned
additional_senses.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text (Wang Bi recension)
Sentence Translations (English): This can be known.
That is hard to name.
What is above is honored, what is below is lowly.
This is the constant.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): a nominalizing particle after a demonstrative or numeral that turns the preceding phrase into a substantive reference
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text (Wang Bi recension)

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): describes a pleasing appearance or a thing that looks fine
additional_senses.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text (Wang Bi recension)
Sentence Translations (English): That person is very beautiful.
The flowers are extremely lovely in color.
The vessel is finely made.
The mountains and streams are clear and beautiful.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): treats something as beautiful or worthy of admiration
additional_senses.Register (English): Classical Chinese; literary
Sentence Translations (English): All praised it.
Many praised his conduct.
The minister did not dare to use flattering words.
Only you admire that man.
additional_senses.Translation (English): to praise as beautiful; to admire

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): the quality, thing, or standard regarded as beautiful
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text (Wang Bi recension)

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): indicates an action performed or an act of making something
additional_senses.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text (Wang Bi recension)
Sentence Translations (English): The ruler does good.
The minister speaks.
The craftsman makes implements.
I do this.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): shows that someone or something functions in a role or capacity
additional_senses.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text (Wang Bi recension)
Sentence Translations (English): Take humaneness as the root.
Take ritual as instruction.
The people serve as the foundation of the state.
Water serves as a mirror.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): expresses classification or judgment, presenting one thing as being treated as another
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text (Wang Bi recension)
contextual_sense.Translation (English): to be regarded as; to be taken for

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): describes something that looks unpleasant or lacks beauty
additional_senses.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text (Wang Bi recension)
Sentence Translations (English): Its appearance is very ugly.
His face has a rough and unsightly look.
The clothing and bearing are coarse and ugly.
The rocks in the mountains are steep and ugly.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): describes moral wrongness, harmfulness, or wicked behavior
additional_senses.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text (Wang Bi recension)
Sentence Translations (English): To act without goodness is evil.
His heart is very wicked.
Those who do evil fail.
Evil is where all evils gather.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): the quality, thing, or standard regarded as ugly or unsightly
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text (Wang Bi recension)

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): language, utterance, or the wording of a statement
additional_senses.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text (Wang Bi recension)
Sentence Translations (English): His words are plain.
Fine words move people.
Straightforward speech is easy to trust.
Ancient wording can be recited.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): a formal goodbye or departure from someone or somewhere
additional_senses.Register (English): Classical Chinese; literary
Sentence Translations (English): At departure he made his farewells.
You came without taking leave.
The guest rose and took his leave.
After the meeting was over, he departed.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): turns down, rejects, or does not accept something offered or implied
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): refusal of an offer or claim
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text (Wang Bi recension)

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): reside in a place or stay somewhere
additional_senses.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text (Wang Bi recension)
Sentence Translations (English): The hermit dwells in the mountains.
Father and son live together.
Many people are unsettled in their homes.
The guest is staying here temporarily.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): keeps or occupies a position, space, office, or rank
additional_senses.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text (Wang Bi recension)
Sentence Translations (English): The army occupies the high position.
The troops occupy a dangerous place.
The worthy man holds his office.
North of the city, the ground is high.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): takes possession of an achievement or rests on it as one’s own merit
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text (Wang Bi recension)

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): an adult male, or specifically a husband
additional_senses.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text (Wang Bi recension)
Sentence Translations (English): Her husband has returned.
The old man is here.
A good man keeps righteousness.
The wife thinks of her husband.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): a male person in a lower or ordinary social role
additional_senses.Register (English): Classical Chinese; literary
Sentence Translations (English): One soldier guards the pass.
Every man has responsibility.
Common men perform service.
There are no resentful men in the state.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): an introductory discourse particle that marks emphasis or sets up the following judgment
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text (Wang Bi recension)

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): beholds something with the eyes or notices it mentally
additional_senses.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text (Wang Bi recension)
Sentence Translations (English): I see that man.
The distant mountains are visible.
Do you not see it?
All are able to see it.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): comes into view or becomes visible
additional_senses.Register (English): Classical Chinese; literary
Sentence Translations (English): The sun rises and appears.
When the clouds clear, the peak is seen.
His reputation then became visible.
A faint light has just appeared.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): causes something to be seen or made visible to others
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text (Wang Bi recension)

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): the shared mental and emotional disposition of the populace as a collective
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text (Wang Bi recension)

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): persons characterized by wisdom or shrewd intelligence
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text (Wang Bi recension)

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): moves quickly or violently forward, or rises in a forceful wave
additional_senses.Register (English): Classical Chinese; literary
Sentence Translations (English): The tide surges against the shore.
The carts and horses rush forward.
Anger surges up.
The waterfall plunges straight down.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): cleans by running liquid through or over something
additional_senses.Register (English): Classical Chinese; literary
Sentence Translations (English): Rinse away the dust with water.
First rinse the vessel.
After the rain, the road can be washed clean.
Well water can cool away the heat.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): lacking fullness; open or not packed tight, as a vessel or space may be
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): in Laozi, a positive image of openness rather than deficiency
contextual_sense.Register (English): Classical Chinese; received Laozi text (Wang Bi recension)
